items.title: Meta Ads: $48.17 spend, 5 leads, $9.63 CPL — Flooring Problems Campaign
items.summary: Yesterday (2026-09-07) Meta spent $48.17, all on the sole actively-delivering campaign, Flooring Problems Campaign, generating 5 leads at $9.63 CPL. That's well under the 7-day baseline (2026-09-01 to 2026-09-07: $335.93 / 24 leads, ~$14.00 CPL), so no anomaly; account is ACTIVE and no ads are flagged.

needs_attention: Flooring Problems Campaign's raw actions again include lead-like conversion types outside the script's documented LEAD_ACTION_TYPES set (offsite_complete_registration_add_meta_leads, offsite_search_add_meta_leads, offsite_content_view_add_meta_leads — each valued at 5, matching the counted leads exactly, same as flagged on 2026-08-31, 2026-09-02, and 2026-09-07). No discrepancy in the counted total so far, but this is now the fourth consecutive run seeing it — the script's lead-action set should be extended rather than continuing to hand-note it.

This branch's own ingest/ history only shows a prior meta-ads.json through 2026-09-02 (a known branch-isolation artifact — daily-ingest runs for 2026-09-03 through 2026-09-07 landed on separate unmerged session branches: adoring-mendel-i23iun, -855vhn, -3rgf82, -pccybs, -gs75gw respectively). Confirmed via cross-branch check that 2026-09-07's run completed normally and its window already covered through 2026-09-06, so today's pull correctly used the standard 1-day window (2026-09-07) with no gap to widen.
